\section[resolver]{resolver — to solve, to sort out}

\label{lesson:ES-C481-resolver}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to promise, then the Spanish for to complain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: resolver}
\textbf{resolver} — \textquotedblleft{}to solve, to sort out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Vamos a resolver el problema hoy.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are going to sort out the problem today.}
\end{quote}

The o breaks into ue under stress: \emph{resuelvo}, \emph{resuelve}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{resolver}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{resolver}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{resolver}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to promise, then the Spanish for to complain, then say \emph{resolver} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does resolver mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To solve, to sort out\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[recuperar]{recuperar — to get back, to recover}

\label{lesson:ES-C481-recuperar}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: recuperar}

\section[prever]{prever — to foresee, to expect}

\label{lesson:ES-C481-prever}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to get back, then the Spanish for to rule out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: prever}
\textbf{prever} — \textquotedblleft{}to foresee, to expect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rain is expected for the weekend.}
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{ver}, and conjugated like it: \emph{preveo}, \emph{prevé}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.

\section[vigilar]{vigilar — to watch, to keep an eye on}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to rule out, then the Spanish for to foresee.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: vigilar}
\textbf{vigilar} — \textquotedblleft{}to watch, to keep an eye on\textquotedblright{}.

\end{quote}

\emph{Zona vigilada} on a sign means the area is watched.
